svg.title: Shirudo on an Azure Trusted Launch VM: Experimental Architecture, Three Key Roles, and Trust Boundaries
svg.desc: Architecture diagram showing two separate VMs in an independent experimental Azure port of Shirudo. On the left, the Operator VM (Standard_D32ds_v5, Trusted Launch with vTPM on and Secure Boot on) holds separate private ML-DSA-87 bpf and config signing keypairs (key role 1), builds the Hyper-V enabled bpf-next kernel and RSA-2048 NV writer compatibility packages, delivers signed artifacts via workstation SSH relay or Azure VM Run Command, and runs before-and-after fresh-nonce offline attestation verification (checking PCR 13 signed config root, rejecting a wrong nonce, and verifying baseline plus planned signed transitions). On the right, the Azure Trusted Launch Target VM (Standard_D4ds_v5, base image 26.04.202611100, custom kernel 7.4-shirudo-azure-20261124, vTPM on, Secure Boot off, unsigned UKI, no inbound app ports) shows four layers: unauthenticated early boot/initrd, the running kernel's sealed keyrings and pinned lsm/bpf guard (denying unsigned BPF load, map mutation, and link detach during this boot, not a boot or Azure-admin boundary), target userspace status and Java startup agents, and the Microsoft Hyper-V vTPM holding the RSA-2048 NV writer primary key (key role 3) and separate Azure RBAC TOFU ECDSA P-256 attestation key (key role 2, proving state and transitions without EK endorsement or whole-history operator-intent assurance). Managed AKS, real PHP-FPM/H2 supplement (pending), application overhead benchmarks, and IG are marked separate or out of tested scope.
